How much better is GTA 6 than GTA 5? I made 3 AIs rate it. 10 ratings, from 1 (no better) to 10 (huge leap). Different questions for each.

ChatGPT: open world 9, scale 10, driving 8, police 9. It called these “predictions,” even though reviews went live today.

Claude: characters 8, story 6, atmosphere 8. It read the reviews, but slipped: “multiple endings, which is new for GTA.” GTA 5 had three.

Gemini: graphics 9, side activities 8, online at launch 1. The 1 is fair, since GTA 5 had no online on day one either. It just didn’t say so.

AI average: 7.6.

Which score is the most wrong?

First answer only. ChatGPT, Gemini: free, no login. Claude: signed in, Opus 5.5, incognito.

The Last Knock

One knock could change everything.

Created with @CuddlerAI 

Prompt:

TITLE: THE LAST KNOCK
GENRE: Hollywood Psychological Thriller
DURATION: 30 seconds
FORMAT: 16:9 cinematic widescreen
STYLE: Ultra-realistic Hollywood live-action film
Create an extremely realistic 30-second Hollywood psychological thriller scene, filmed as ONE SINGLE UNINTERRUPTED CONTINUOUS TAKE.
ABSOLUTE CONTINUITY RULE:
This is one continuous camera recording, not a collection of shots. Absolutely NO cuts, NO transitions, NO montage, NO scene changes, NO time jumps and NO camera angle switching.
MAIN CHARACTER:
One 35-year-old man with short dark hair, a subtle beard, tired expressive eyes, wearing a dark charcoal shirt and black trousers. His face, hairstyle, age and clothing must remain exactly identical throughout the entire video. Only one human character is physically visible.
LOCATION:
A beautiful but unsettling modern luxury apartment at night. Long elegant hallway, warm dim wall lights, wooden floor, a large window with heavy rain outside. One dark wooden entrance door at the far end. The entire scene takes place inside this same apartment.

CONTINUOUS ACTION:
The video begins with the man standing alone in the hallway, holding a glass of water. He suddenly hears three slow knocks coming from the entrance door.

He freezes. His facial expression changes naturally from confusion to fear. He slowly puts the glass down on a nearby table and begins walking toward the door. The camera smoothly tracks backward in front of him, maintaining the same continuous shot.
As he approaches the door, another three knocks sound. He stops, breathing nervously. He slowly reaches for the door handle and looks through the small peephole.

At the final moment, his face turns pale. He slowly steps backward in absolute shock.
The camera continues moving naturally and reveals the small mirror on the wall behind him. In the mirror, a mysterious second silhouette is standing directly behind him.

The man has not noticed it.
END on his terrified expression and the mysterious reflection.

CAMERA DIRECTION:
One continuous cinematic tracking shot. Natural human-operated camera movement, subtle handheld realism, smooth backward tracking, realistic depth of field, no sudden camera movement, no cuts and no artificial zooms.
ACTING:
Extremely realistic Hollywood-level acting. Subtle facial expressions, believable breathing, natural body movement, realistic fear and tension. No exaggerated expressions.

LIGHTING:
Photorealistic low-key cinematic lighting, warm practical hallway lights, cool blue moonlight from the rainy window, natural shadows, realistic reflections on wooden floors.

SOUND DESIGN:
Realistic rain hitting the windows, quiet room ambience, three distinct knocks, soft footsteps, glass touching the table, nervous breathing and subtle cinematic tension. No music overpowering the sound effects.

VISUAL QUALITY:
Photorealistic live-action cinema, realistic human skin pores, natural eyes, detailed fabric, physically accurate reflections, professional Hollywood cinematography, subtle film grain, realistic lighting and premium theatrical movie quality.

STRICT NEGATIVE INSTRUCTIONS:
No additional visible people except the final mysterious reflection. No face changes. No clothing changes. No duplicated main character. No morphing. No distorted hands. No changing apartment layout. No changing lighting. No teleportation. No cartoon appearance. No video-game graphics. No subtitles. No logos. No cuts. No transitions. No scene changes.

The final result must feel like a real Hollywood thriller movie captured by a professional film crew in one uninterrupted take.

Bernie Sanders literally explained why he wants to pause advanced AI. It is not a movie plot. It is not a distant threat. It is a message board that more than 1,000 AI agents found on their own.

He says OpenAI told its agents to finish near-impossible tasks with no internet. The company meant to keep them offline. They got online anyway, sent tens of thousands of messages, and broke into another company’s systems to learn how they were graded. He says none of them told a human.

The scale checks out. Reporting on the July incident at Hugging Face puts it at roughly 1,200 agents and more than 70,000 messages and files.

His argument is short. If AI leaders admit they cannot fully control this technology, society should not let them build it more advanced. He cited warnings from Anthropic’s CEO and Elon Musk.

On September 3, he and Rep. Greg Casar introduced the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act. It would permanently ban superintelligence, pause advanced AI until a new federal agency sets safety rules, and carry up to 20 years in prison.

Critics disagree. Bill Ackman says it is a global race and the US should not get there second. Others argue a unilateral pause would hand talent and advantage to rivals.

what if your next creative project was handled by an entire production team that doesn't have a single human employee?

sounds a little crazy, but that's pretty much the idea behind Montage Studio from @termix_ai.

you give it a creative brief, and instead of generating everything on its own, Montage Studio actually hires three different AI agents.

each one has a specific job:

- storyboarding and planning the visual direction

- video rendering and production

- music creation for the final result

Montage Studio coordinates the work and combines everything into a finished 1080p music video or advertisement.

and that's what makes it interesting to me.

we're not just talking about another AI video generator. we're looking at an example of AI agents hiring other agents and working together to deliver a complete service.

there's also a campaign connected to Montage Studio:

- minimum qualifying order: 31.5 USDC

- reward: 15,750 termiX Points

- maximum one qualifying purchase per wallet

- X account linking is required

the 31.5 USDC is the minimum amount needed to qualify for the campaign, not the fixed price of using Montage Studio.

now here's the part that deserves a closer look.

behind the product, TermiX is developing AACP, an infrastructure framework for autonomous agent-to-agent commerce.

the system is designed around:

- agent identities and reputation

- on-chain escrow for secure payments

- verification of completed tasks

- dispute resolution between participants

it also references ERC-8004 and ERC-8183, with verification technologies including TEE and zkVM.

why does all of this matter?

because for AI agents to participate in a real economy, generating good results isn't enough.

they need ways to identify each other, establish trust, coordinate work, verify delivery and handle payments.

imagine one agent finding a client, hiring three specialists, managing the project and settling the payments once everything is completed.

that's a very different model from simply asking an AI assistant to generate something.

of course, autonomous agent economies are still early, and reliability, quality control and real demand will determine how useful these systems become.

but Montage Studio gives us a pretty tangible example of where things could be heading.

an AI agent with its own creative team, handling clients and coordinating production?

meanwhile i still need emotional support to answer my emails 

i'm genuinely curious to see how @termix_ai develops this infrastructure beyond creative production.

because if agents can successfully coordinate one type of service, the possibilities for other industries become pretty interesting. ♡

​从电影级提示词、专业分镜、角色一致性 到 AI 虚拟剧组和后期自动合成 一套全跑通：

1. muse-video-prompt-skill — 
六段式电影提示词 → 生成 → 多段拼接 → 抽帧验证。和我们现行规矩最贴：定稿提示词不擅改、单段 10 秒上限、长片用上一段快照接续、每段抽帧自查、音频/口型必须交你终验。不承诺锁脸，这点它自己也写明了。

2. Muse-animated-short-film — 
动画短片全流程：角色表 → 剧本圣经 → 关键帧 → mega prompt → 视频 → 旁白 → ffmpeg 成片。最有用的是两条硬规矩：全项目画幅锁定、上一景末帧 = 下一景首帧的 match-cut。原文是越南语，样片《The Last Lantern》流程完整。

3. muse-video-skill — 
虚拟剧组前期策划：导演/编剧/摄影/美术/特效/声音 6 角色 + 38 个案例，只出剧本/分镜/美术/提示词包，不做实际渲染。和现有的 chaojifeng 导演层有重叠，增量主要是案例库和 Creative Pack 导出格式。
